chunks: I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام asking him about the Imam, whether he experiences wet dreams. And I said to myself after the letter had been sent: “Wet dreams are from Satan, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has protected His Awliyā’ from that.”

So the reply came: “The state of the Imams عليهم السلام in sleep is their state in wakefulness. Sleep does not change anything in them, and Allah has protected His Awliyā’ from the touch of Satan, just as your own self told you.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءَهُ: His Awliyā’, meaning those under Allah’s special guardianship
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams, referring to the divinely guided leaders from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader being asked about here
key_terms.الْمَنَامِ: sleep or the state of sleeping
key_terms.لَمَّةِ الشَّيْطَانِ: the touch, suggestion, or assault of Satan

ai.seo_question: Do the Imams عليهم السلام experience satanic wet dreams during sleep?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms a theological distinction of the Imams عليهم السلام: their state in sleep remains like their state in wakefulness, without deficiency or satanic interference. It presents divine protection of Allah’s Awliyā’ from satanic touch and supports the doctrine of their purity and safeguarded condition.

en.hubeali: Is’haq, from Al Aqra’a who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the Imam<sup>asws</sup> whether he<sup>asws</sup> would experience wet dreams, and I said within myself after sending the letter, ‘The wet dreams are Satanic and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High has Sheltered His<sup>azwj</sup> Guardians<sup>asws</sup> from that’.

So the answer came, ‘The state of the Imams<sup>asws</sup> during the sleep is their<sup>asws</sup> state during the wakefulness. The sleep does not change anything from them<sup>asws</sup>, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Sheltered His<sup>azwj</sup> Guardians<sup>asws</sup> from the ordeal of the Satan<sup>la</sup> just as you discussed with yourself’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ishaq has narrated from al-Aqra‘ who has said the following.

“I wrote to abu Muhammad (a.s.) asking him if Imams experience wet dreams? I said to myself after the letter had gone, “Wet dream is something Satanic, and Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has protected those whom He has given authority against such things.”

The answer came. “The conditions of the Imams when asleep is the same as when they are awake. Sleep does not change anything in them. Allah has given protection to those whom He has given authority from Satanic encounters as you spoke to yourself.”
